clue.text: With extraordinary charm, old capital smothers a censor

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so the letters of charm and old are put out of their usual order
to smother is to cover over, so the capital wraps itself round the a

parts.note: Berlin is the capital of Germany

explanation.surface: With remarkable charm, an old city muffles the official who bans things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' signals the anagram and 'smothers' the container. 'old' seems to describe the capital but is anagram fodder, and the Lord Chamberlain censored British plays until 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chamberlain licensed British stage plays and acted as theatre censor until 1968.

clue.text: Crave drug from receiver of kicks?

parts.note: to crave something is to long for it
grass is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone yearning for a fix from a rough-housing customer.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'kick something into the long grass' is a British idiom for shelving a problem indefinitely, so the long grass receives the kicks.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: awkward issues are kicked into tall uncut vegetation to be forgotten, so it receives kicks.

clue.text: Sport that is newly put in store

indicators.note: newly suggests the letters are made over afresh into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A game which has just been put away in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges SPORT plus IE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposit is a formal verb meaning to deposit or lay something away for safekeeping.

clue.text: Smart lad's victims of premature count?

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish
Ken is a typical lad's name, here with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A stylish boy's targets fell foul of an early tally.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says 'don't count your chickens before they are hatched', so they are the victims of a count made too early.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbial allusion: poultry counted before hatching are the classic example of premature reckoning.

clue.text: Backer of good old coin

definitions.meaning: a theatrical investor who finances a show
an old English gold coin showing St Michael, a good being

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre backer is called an angel, and the angel was also a medieval English coin.

clue.text: Acknowledges old actor's time with runners

parts.note: a performer bows to acknowledge applause
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: An elderly performer takes his bows and spends his hours with athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bow Street Runners were London's first professional police force, founded by Henry Fielding in 1749; Bow Street is also home to its magistrates' court.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the Bow Street Runners were early London constables named after the street.

clue.text: Island ways being broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: roads are ways

explanation.surface: A holiday isle whose streets are on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a large Greek island in the Dodecanese.

clue.text: Event with lots of bridge?

parts.note: a sale divided into lots, with bids as in the card game

explanation.definitionFit: A sale where goods go in lots to the highest bidder, with bidding also central to bridge.

clue.text: Related to one's origin in South Africa

definitions.meaning: a former province of South Africa

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to birth, and the same name belongs to a South African region.

clue.text: Liable to be detected having forty winks

definitions.meaning: to be caught off guard, as in the idiom about being caught unawares

explanation.definitionFit: Being caught unprepared is being caught napping, and taking a short sleep is also napping.

clue.text: Lumberjack's picture?

parts.note: a print made from a carved block of timber, jokingly credited to someone who fells trees

explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print made from an engraved block of timber, playfully linked to tree felling.

clue.text: Talk of state?

definitions.meaning: one of the states of matter besides solid and liquid

explanation.definitionFit: Gas means empty chatter, and it is also a state of matter alongside solid and liquid.

clue.text: Prevent passing of legislation to reduce police numbers?

definitions.meaning: defeat a proposed act of parliament
the Bill is British slang for the police, and killing it would shrink the force

explanation.definitionFit: Defeating a parliamentary measure is the idiom here; the Old Bill is British slang for police.

clue.text: Reduced borough with David and Richard playing a duet

indicators.note: the clue asks for what goes with borough to make the brothers' surname, so borough is removed from it

parts.note: David and Richard Attenborough, the naturalist broadcaster and the actor-director
taken as written

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of a duet are performed in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A town shrunk when two famous brothers played a piece for two.
explanation.walkthrough: The part that goes 'with' borough to make the Attenborough brothers' name is ATTEN; 'playing' rearranges A DUET into UATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Attenuated means made thinner or weaker, a synonym of reduced.

clue.text: A mutiny to elevate atmosphere at the 28?

parts.note: UDI, a unilateral declaration of independence, is a rebellion against authority

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it to read upwards

parts.note: air means atmosphere

explanation.surface: A rebellion to lift the mood at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevate' turns AIR upwards to give RIA. UDI was Rhodesia's 1965 break from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Theatre holds three auditoria, the halls where an audience sits.

clue.text: Kings keeping tips on account may be taken aback

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the kings surround the rest

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, twice here
a nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection

explanation.surface: Monarchs holding gratuities on credit might be startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be taken aback' reads as being startled but means carried on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A knapsack is a bag carried on the back, so it may be taken on one's back.

clue.text: God's in attitude that will give a speedy ride

definitions.text: that will give a speedy ride

indicators.note: in places the god's name within the attitude

parts.note: a pose is a bodily attitude
Thor is the Norse god of thunder, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A deity strikes a pose that promises a fast trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Post horses were kept at staging posts for swift relays of riders or mail coaches.

clue.text: Poet-parson upset Cleo

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word over so it reads upwards

parts.note: Rev, short for reverend, is a parson
Cleo Laine was a British jazz singer

explanation.surface: A versifying clergyman has unsettled Cleopatra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals the upward reading in this down clue. Cleo Laine was a famous British jazz singer, so 'Cleo' is not Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Verlaine was a nineteenth-century French Symbolist poet.

clue.text: See 15
Incest upsetting sick musician

annotationWithheld.why: Incest upsetting sick musician (7): the parse is CE(LLI)ST with ILL reversed placed 'in' CEST, splitting the single word 'Incest' into the indicator 'In' and fodder CEST, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: Actor in the front inside back

indicators.note: in places the front within the reversed side
back tells us to read the side the other way round

parts.note: split as in-side, the side part supplying the letters
the van is the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A performer seated at the front, inside the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SIDE (from in-side) into EDIS, and THE VAN goes in it. Dame Edith Evans was a great English actress; actor covers both sexes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edith Evans was a celebrated English stage and film performer, famed as Lady Bracknell.

clue.text: In painting, an encore given to such as Lawrence

indicators.note: In places the other pieces within the painting

parts.note: painting is art
bis is a call for an encore, Latin for twice

explanation.surface: An artwork receives a repeat performance for an admirer of Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia', was an expert in Arab affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabist is a specialist in Arab culture and language, as T. E. Lawrence was.

clue.text: Wodehousian greeting to doctor without cover

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the doctor surrounds the cover

parts.note: Doctor Who, the time-travelling television character
a hat is a head covering

explanation.surface: Hailing a physician who has lost his lid, as in a comic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: the doctor goes round the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: This hearty hail is the trademark salutation of P. G. Wodehouse's Bertie Wooster.

clue.text: Play throughout the season in question with everyone going down

definitions.meaning: a radio drama by Samuel Beckett
for the whole of that autumn, fall being American for autumn
all who tumble, as in the hymn phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Beckett wrote the radio play; the words also mean all of that autumn, or everyone who tumbles.

clue.text: Shaker when writer?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Asking whether a trembler is the one doing the writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The aspen is the trembling poplar, whose leaves quiver in the slightest breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen tree's leaves flutter constantly, so it is known for shaking.

clue.text: A fight, more or less

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.definitionFit: About means approximately, roughly the same as more or less.

clue.text: Keyholder having been fired?

definitions.meaning: the tree whose winged seeds are called keys
the powdery residue left when something burns

explanation.definitionFit: The ash tree bears seeds known as keys, and ash is also what remains after burning.

clue.text: Artist, one writing plays for adults included

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so the adults go within the playwright

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright
A is the film certificate for adults

explanation.surface: A creative person who writes drama with grown-ups in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: A was the old British film certificate for adults.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is a visual artist working in oils or watercolours.

clue.text: One in musical — "The Prince and the Showgirl"?

indicators.note: in places the one within the musical

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single person in a stage show, perhaps that Marilyn Monroe film.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier directed and starred in the 1957 film with Marilyn Monroe; one of the National Theatre's auditoria bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier directed and co-starred in that film, so the title stands for its maker.

clue.text: I enter alliance with Lovelace's new girl, rendering three — which includes 27

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the I goes within the alliance

parts.note: NATO, the North Atlantic alliance
N for new, then Althea, addressee of Richard Lovelace's poem To Althea, from Prison
tre is three rendered into Italian

explanation.surface: A convoluted sentence about joining a pact with a poet's latest sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' signals the container; 'rendering' means translating, so three goes into Italian. The National Theatre's three auditoria are the Olivier, Lyttelton and Cottesloe.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Theatre on London's South Bank contains the Olivier as one of its auditoria.
